newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes weak, lingering Gulf barrels trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes weak, lingering Gulf barrels trade.

text.p: Crude prices in Asia fell further on Wednesday in the wake bout of weakness in global futures.
The values for Brent/Dubai on December came in flat or in a slight contango to January in Asian hours, after the tumble in dated Brent values in Europe on Tuesday.
December was assessed around $2.12, while January was around $2.10. Early Europe reported similar values.
The potential for narrowing the Brent/Dubai and ongoing weak refining margins for middle distillate rich grades has thrown the spotlight on valuation for light sweet grades.
Some traders said the Tapis market for December was more like $1.20/$1.30 based on refinery values for the benchmark crude.
But others noted that producer Petronas is unlikely to have many spot cargoes available and Indonesian availability could be tight.
A major is expected to keep a Cossack cargo in-house, so placing the last December Cossack. That leaves a Griffin, Kutubu and North West Shelf left for December light Australian cargoes.
That could support the Tapis differential, although it was unlikely to push it out further.
Bangchak was still negotiating for the purchase of a Tapis cargo in the wake of last week's December crude buying tender, refining sources said.
Traders said a Japanese refinery bought 500,000 barrels of Lower Zakum at ADNOC +30 cents and 200,000 barrels of Murban at ADNOC +37 cents. Lower Zakum had traded as high as +60 cents for December.
Elsewhere, 500,000 barrels of Masila was said traded Tuesday between a European major and a Korean refiner at dated Brent less $1.25.
